name: ESP32-C6 GEO IMU fusion benchmark
summary: A deterministic six-path replay benchmark compares generic and sparse-fused GEO float/Q16 schedules with conventional quaternion and quantized TinyML baselines.

name: ESP32-C6 IMU fusion benchmark 2026-07-17
summary: A1 reduced A0 latency by 71.71% and reached measurement-level parity with C; all six paths completed 30 runs with zero deadline misses, zero NaNs, and stable hashes.

name: Clean and reproduce the ESP32-C6 GEO IMU fusion benchmark
summary: The validated benchmark has been transplanted to a minimal main-based branch; exact clean-branch build and physical reproduction remain pending.

name: Apply sparse fusion before backend emission
summary: Known-zero grade terms and temporary representation work must be eliminated and accumulations fused before float or fixed backend emission.

name: Sub-microsecond A1/C parity resolution
summary: The 0.095% A1/C difference is below the resolution and experimental controls needed for a robust speed-lead claim.

name: IMU sparse schedule generator
summary: A validated polynomial schedule IR deterministically emits floating helpers and Q32 accumulator helpers now used by the fused IMU runtime source; physical hash and timing validation remain pending.

name: Generate ESP32 IMU sparse schedules automatically
summary: The schedule IR, deterministic generator, generated header, host tests, firmware startup checks, and A1/B1 runtime integration are implemented; local physical hash and timing validation remain.

name: Geometric Identity and Counterexample Engine
summary: A checked Clifford identity IR compiles into exact modular host and CUDA evaluators. V1 was physically validated; v2 adds exact blade-wise polynomial certificates, deterministic mutations, multi-prime expansion, and witness reduction.

name: Build a geometric identity and counterexample engine
summary: The v1 compiler, exact host/CUDA evaluators, corpus, GPU search, CPU witness reproduction, validator, and evidence package passed physical validation across 5,242,880 exact modular assignments.

name: Use exact modular search before symbolic proof
summary: Candidate identities are stress-tested over exact finite fields and false mutations must yield reproducible witnesses before symbolic or formal proof work.

name: Geometric identity engine CUDA validation 2026-07-17
summary: Five statements were evaluated over 5,242,880 exact modular assignments; three known identities survived, two false mutations produced exact assignment-zero witnesses, and validation passed at an aggregate 688.16 million assignments per second.

name: Add multi-prime discovery and witness reduction
summary: V2 deterministically generates one-edit identity mutations, extracts exact blade-wise integer polynomials, expands a prime matrix, compiles manifest corpora, reduces exact witnesses, and aggregates discovery evidence; physical CUDA validation remains.

name: Classify canonical polynomial difference before sampled search
summary: Each statement is first expanded into an exact blade-wise integer polynomial. Zero polynomials are formal identities for the declared structural setting; nonzero polynomials are routed to finite-field witness search.
